title: Evidence Must Govern Vietnam’s Dog-Trade Reform
excerpt: Stolen-pet claims and rabies risks demand proof, quarantine, and accountability. Vietnam needs transparent records—and abolition of dog-meat trade by 2030.
body_html:
One bite from an infected animal can begin a race against time. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Once symptoms appear, it is virtually 100% fatal. Immediate washing with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, followed by urgent medical assessment and post-exposure prophylaxis when indicated, can prevent that outcome. This public-health reality demands evidence—not slogans.

Myths cannot replace records

Claims about cyanide bait, stolen family companions, secret transport, or “farm-raised dogs” require police reports, court judgments, veterinary records, seizure inventories, and named locations. No such incident record appears in current campaign material. That gap does not prove claims false. It means responsible reporting must not present them as established fact.

Likewise, no verified source here proves that Vietnam has no dog farms or that every animal in trade comes from stolen households. Those are testable claims. Authorities should publish transport permits, quarantine records, inspection results, slaughter-site registrations, seizure outcomes, and convictions involving pet theft or animal cruelty.

Biosecurity has no cultural scapegoat

Household rabies exposure and commercial animal transport are parallel biosecurity concerns, not automatically one causal chain. Sick animals, bite attacks, uninspected slaughter, and failed quarantine can endanger communities. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. Anger belongs with criminal operators and enforcement failures—not Vietnamese families, culture, or ethnicity.

WHO guidance on rabies sets the medical standard: wash wounds immediately and seek urgent care before symptoms develop. Vietnam’s public institutions should apply the same seriousness to animal transport, quarantine, theft investigations, and inspection.

Demand proof. Demand abolition.

Vietnamese communities can lead reform that protects families, pets, and public health. SDE’s demand goes beyond any single raid or health alert: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for transparent enforcement, stronger biosecurity, and lasting legal change.

telegram_message:
A missing evidence trail cannot protect a dangerous trade.

• Current campaign material provides no verified police seizure, court judgment, named location, or official dataset confirming claims about cyanide bait, stolen pets, or “farm-raised dogs.” Those claims need records before publication as fact.
• Rabies spreads through infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes—not through properly cooked meat as an established route.
• After possible exposure: wash with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical assessment for vaccination and immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies when indicated.
• Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal.
• Household exposure and commercial transport remain separate biosecurity dimensions unless evidence proves a direct link.

Vietnam needs published quarantine, transport, inspection, theft, and cruelty records. SDE demands complete abolition by 2030.
